text: To fix the worst traffic jam in the city,
an engineer wanted to blow up its busiest highway.
It all started when the city built the skyway,
six lanes of highway slicing straight through downtown.
It was supposed to be the great shortcut.
Instead, a 5-mile drive now takes 45 minutes.
Ambulances sit in traffic with their sirens screaming.
Pizza shows up cold.
Whole marriages end in the left lane.
So the city hires a new traffic engineer, and he does what any sane person would do.
He sits on a bridge above the skyway every morning with a stopwatch and a notebook,
but he doesn't time the skyway.
He times the little side streets nobody uses,
and the only weird thing he ever writes down is this:
Every single driver takes the shortcut every single time.
Then he walks into City Hall with his plan.
Tear the skyway down. All of it.
The council laughs so hard somebody spills coffee on the budget.
One guy leans into his microphone and goes, 'Great idea!
And to fix hunger, we'll close the restaurants.'
The engineer just smiles and says,
'Same cars, fewer roads.'
By the end of the month, he's famous, and not in a good way.
The newspaper draws him holding a stick of dynamite with a traffic cone on his head.
Radio hosts call him the anti-road guy.
Strangers honk at him—he's walking, by the way, they honk anyway.
Now, here's the weird part: everybody figures he secretly hates cars,
that he wants people on buses and bikes.
He doesn't.
He doesn't want a single car off the road.
He wants the exact same traffic on fewer roads,
and somehow he thinks that'll make it faster.
How is that possible?
Meanwhile, the city doubles down.
The council votes to widen the skyway to 8 lanes.
Cranes everywhere, detours everywhere.
The engineer gets moved to a desk in the basement
next to the broken copier.
His boss drops a cardboard box on his desk and goes,
'Take your stopwatch. You've got time to kill.
It's over. The skyway won.'
Then one morning,
a water main bursts right under the skyway.
The whole highway shuts down, no warning.
and no shortcut.
The city braces for the worst traffic jam in its history.
It never comes.
Cars spill onto the side streets and just keep moving.
Ambulances arrive early.
The 5-mile drive takes 15 minutes.
Down in the basement, a stopwatch clicks.
Nobody's laughing anymore.
You see, every driver picks the road that's fastest for them,
not the road that's fastest for everyone.
So when there's one big shortcut, everybody piles onto it at once
and jams every street that feeds it.
Take the shortcut away, and the same cars spread out
over all those empty side streets.
It's like a stadium where everyone sprints for one giant gate
while five side doors sit wide open.
It's called Braess's Paradox.
And in real life, Seoul tore down a downtown highway,
put a stream there, and traffic actually got faster.
The fastest way across town:
blowing up the fastest way across town.
